cities.base: San Telmo or Recoleta, both walkable to the sights and with real restaurant streets for the evenings
cities.name: Buenos Aires

cities.base: Puerto Iguazú town, the only real base for the Argentine side of the park
cities.name: Puerto Iguazú

places.name: Recoleta Cemetery
places.note: Smaller than the photos suggest but the mausoleums are genuinely worth the hour and a half.

places.name: MALBA
places.note: Skip it if the schedule is tight, keep it if modern Latin American art actually interests you.

places.name: La Boca / Caminito
places.note: Daylight only, and don't wander past the four painted blocks.

places.name: San Telmo evening walk and dinner
places.note: No hard sightseeing this first night, just walk and eat while the jet lag wears off.

places.name: Tango dinner show
places.note: Touristy by nature but it's the one night to do it.

places.name: San Telmo antiques market
places.note: Only worth timing for if your slack day lands on a Sunday.

places.name: Steakhouse dinner
places.note: Save this for the last night, not the jet-lagged first one.

places.name: Garganta del Diablo
places.note: Go before 11am or you're on the catwalk with every tour bus in Misiones.

places.name: San Telmo
places.note: Cobblestone streets and old facades, good first evening walk to shake off a flight without demanding much of you.

places.name: Feria de San Telmo (Plaza Dorrego antiques market)
places.note: Sunday only. Antiques, tango buskers, crowded, worth it if your slack day lands on a Sunday, skip otherwise.

places.name: Recoleta Cemetery
places.note: Smaller than the photos suggest but the mausoleums, including Evita's, are genuinely worth the walk.

places.name: MALBA
places.note: Closed Tuesdays. Skip if you're tight on time, keep if you like modern Latin American art.

places.name: Palermo Soho
places.note: Tree lined streets, independent designers, cafes. Better for wandering without an itinerary than for any single sight.

places.name: La Boca / Caminito
places.note: Free to walk, souvenirs extra. Daylight only and stick to the four painted blocks, the surrounding area is not safe to wander into.

places.name: Cafe de los Angelitos
places.note: Dinner and tango show in a historic cafe. Touristy but well run, book ahead, pricier packages include better seats.

places.name: Don Julio
places.note: Widely regarded as the best classic parrilla in the city, reserve well in advance or expect a long wait.

places.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
places.note: Old theater converted into a bookstore, worth a quick look for the architecture even if you don't read Spanish.

places.name: Obelisco / Avenida 9 de Julio
places.note: Skip lingering here, it's a photo stop on the way between neighborhoods, not a destination in itself.

places.name: Cafe Tortoni
places.note: Oldest cafe in the city, ornate interior, coffee is average and service is rushed given the tour bus traffic.

places.name: Mercado de San Telmo
places.note: Iron and glass market hall from 1897, good for an empanada or a coffee break between antiques stalls.

places.name: Garganta del Diablo
places.note: Little train plus a 1km walkway over the river to the main drop. Go before 11am, it's a single walkway and gets clogged with tour buses by midday, and you get soaked in the spray regardless of dry season.

places.name: Circuito Superior
places.note: Flat walkway along the top edge of a string of falls, looking down. Included in park entry, easy to combine with Circuito Inferior same day.

places.name: Circuito Inferior
places.note: Lower trail with stairs down toward river level, better face-on views of the falls than the upper circuit, ends at the dock for Isla San Martín.

places.name: Isla San Martín
places.note: Short free boat crossing then a scramble up rocky paths to viewpoints facing several falls at once. Closes when the river is running high, no warning given in advance.

places.name: Gran Aventura boat ride
places.note: Truck ride through jungle then a speedboat that drives straight into the base of the falls. Genuinely fun, not a token soak, use a dry bag or leave the phone in the locker they rent.

places.name: Sendero Macuco to Salto Arrechea
places.note: Flat jungle trail, about 3.5km each way, ends at a small waterfall you can swim under. Almost nobody on it compared to the main circuits, good for the morning before an afternoon flight.

places.name: Hito Tres Fronteras
places.note: A marker and viewpoint where Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay meet at the confluence of the Iguazú and Paraná rivers. Worth ten minutes at sunset, nothing more, sellers of trinkets nearby.

places.name: Brazilian side panoramic walk (Parque Nacional do Iguaçu)
places.note: Requires crossing the border and, depending on nationality, a Brazilian visa. Gives the wide panoramic shot of the falls the Argentine side can't, but with a 3 night Argentina-only itinerary it doesn't fit, skip unless you've sorted entry paperwork in advance.

places.name: Güira Oga wildlife refuge
places.note: Rescue and rehab center for injured native birds and animals, good rainy-day fallback if the falls trails are miserable underfoot, but it's a consolation prize, not a priority.

places.name: La Rueda 1975
places.note: Long-running parrilla in town, good river fish (surubí) as well as steak, reliable choice for one of the three Iguazú dinners without needing a car.

places.name: Jardín de los Picaflores
places.note: Small hummingbird garden, dozens of species buzzing at close range, low key and quick, best combined with the Hito Tres Fronteras on the way back into town.

places.name: Feria Artesanal de Puerto Iguazú
places.note: Small craft market in the town center, mate gourds and yerba, wood carvings. Fine for a last-night browse after dinner, not a destination on its own.

outings.why: Lower boardwalk circuit that gets you close to the base of several falls, and a short boat crossing to the island for a different angle; easy walking, first afternoon material.
outings.name: Circuito Inferior and Isla San Martín

outings.why: A catwalk out over the river to the lip of the biggest drop in the system; go before 11am or you're sharing the platform with every tour bus in Misiones.
outings.name: Garganta del Diablo

outings.why: A boat that drives directly into the spray under the falls; you will get completely soaked, bring a dry bag for anything electronic.
outings.name: Gran Aventura boat ride

outings.why: A flatter jungle trail away from the crowds, ending at a swimmable waterfall; the quiet counterpoint to the two big-ticket days.
outings.name: Sendero Macuco to Salto Arrechea

destination.name: Buenos Aires & Iguazú Falls
destination.pitch: One city, one natural wonder: Buenos Aires bookends three full days at Iguazú, which is the right amount of Argentina for a week.
destination.caveat: The domestic AEP/IGR flight is booked separately from the international EZE ticket and the two airports are across town from each other, so the transfer window is a real cost in time and money, not a formality. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Buenos Aires has the cemeteries, museums, and steak to fill two dense days without repeating itself.
because.food: Steakhouse dinners and San Telmo evenings are the baseline, not a splurge.
because.nature: Iguazú is one of the largest waterfall systems on earth and the Argentine side gets you inside and above it, not just looking at it.
because.culture: Recoleta and the tango dinner give you Argentina's self-image in a single day.
because.adventure: The Gran Aventura boat runs you directly under the falls and Garganta del Diablo puts you on a catwalk over the drop.
